rationale: The recent misses suggest the next move should be a real architectural pivot, not another tiny replay of the same endgame knobs. I kept the current best qk-gain, bigram rank-64 tail, projection-only FP16 keep set, and quant-aware finish intact, then transplanted a lighter parallel-residual/shared-norm block style only into the decoder half. That preserves the stronger existing encoder path while making the output-facing blocks cheaper and less sequential, which should buy slightly more useful decoder updates inside the 600-second cap and test the parallel-residual motif without the heavier sharing changes that already failed. The change is compile-stable, adds no meaningful artifact bytes, removes the now-unused second decoder norm path, and still preserves the exact final int8+zlib roundtrip evaluation path and marker.
title: Decoder Parallel Residual Shared-Norm On Bigram64 Best
